answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may earn rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Creating a hundred fake identities no longer gives an attacker free votes or income: each identity needs its own capital at risk, and coordinated Sybil accounts can lose it all. A lantern may reveal patterns, a plume may signal reputation, and an ember may mark a small stake, but none substitutes for the costly bond.
